note: The sources of the place packs. Every accepted source has an open licence that allows redistribution (checked November 2026; check again when a source changes its terms). url fields marked verify: true were written from the publisher's documented pattern and must be checked at the first build (a failed download only leaves that layer out and is listed in the build summary). Placeholders: {geofabrik} {code} {fips} {pruid} {name} and the settings below.

US-Government-Work.name: Public domain: a work of the United States Government (17 U.S.C. 105)

per-feed-open.name: Each feed's own open licence (Creative Commons BY or zero, ODC-By, PDDL, OGL-Canada, US government works), listed in the pack

per-source-open.name: Each source's own open licence (public domain, CC0, CC BY, ODC-By, OGL), listed in the pack; share-alike and non-commercial sources are left out

PDDL-1.0.name: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License 1.0

public-domain-marked.name: Public domain (marked "Public Domain" by the publishing government's open-data portal)

NYC-Open-Data.name: New York City Open Data: made available without registration, licence requirements or restrictions on use (NYC Administrative Code 23-502(d)); the source and version are named

OPEN-NY.name: New York State OPEN-NY Terms of Use: free use and reuse, no attribution, share-alike or pre-approval required

Newberry-open.name: The Newberry Library's open terms: available for any lawful purpose, commercial or non-commercial, without licensing or permission fees

accepted.name: OpenStreetMap
accepted.attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0: https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
accepted.history: From the first build (November 2026) on. OpenStreetMap's full history is open (ODbL), but per-state history extracts need an OpenStreetMap login at Geofabrik and the full planet history is about 150 GB, so it is not used.

accepted.name: National Address Database (USDOT)
accepted.attribution: Contains address points from the U.S. Department of Transportation's National Address Database, compiled from state, county, city and tribal addressing authorities. Not for use as a mailing list.
accepted.history: From the first build on; earlier NAD releases are added (nad_seed_releases) only if USDOT keeps them openly downloadable. A new release is downloaded only when its file on data.transportation.gov changes (its blobId and rowsUpdatedAt).
accepted.notes: Downloaded from USDOT's data.transportation.gov (dataset fc2s-wawr, the "TXT.zip" file, about 8.5 GB): its address is read from the dataset's metadata at each build, and the old nationaladdressdata S3 bucket (now refusing downloads) is only a fallback. The download is kept in the Actions cache and continues where it stopped after a dropped connection. USDOT marks the data of HI, MI, MN, NH, OR, SC and SD, and parts of CO, IL, KS, MD and ND, as possibly not public domain; those states are left out until their terms are checked. State laws forbid using it as a mailing list; the packs are for naming places in pictures.

accepted.name: Open Database of Addresses (Statistics Canada)
accepted.short: Statistics Canada's Open Database of Addresses
accepted.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada (Statistics Canada, The Open Database of Addresses, and the local authorities listed in its documentation).
accepted.history: One release (2021); later releases are merged as they come.

accepted.name: OpenAddresses
accepted.attribution: Address data from OpenAddresses (openaddresses.io) and the sources listed in the pack, each under its own licence.
accepted.history: From the first build on; OpenAddresses keeps past runs, but its downloads need an account, so they are not fetched automatically.
accepted.notes: Only sources whose licence is public domain, CC0, CC BY, ODC-By or OGL-type are used (allowed_licences); share-alike and non-commercial sources are left out. Mainly for the states the NAD leaves out. Put the source's CSV and its JSON (with the licence) in inputs/openaddresses/<region id>/.

accepted.name: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line places
accepted.attribution: Boundaries from the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles (public domain).
accepted.history: Yearly releases; the current one (seed years possible like the address ranges).

accepted.name: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line county subdivisions
accepted.attribution: Boundaries from the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles (public domain).
accepted.history: Yearly releases; the current one.

accepted.name: US Census Bureau ZIP Code Tabulation Areas
accepted.attribution: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas from the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles (public domain).
accepted.history: The 2020 areas (they change once a decade).

accepted.name: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line address ranges
accepted.short: the US Census Bureau's address ranges
accepted.attribution: Street names and address ranges from the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles (public domain).
accepted.history: Seeded from the yearly releases in tiger_seed_years (every 3 years from 2011, when ADDRFEAT starts), then every year: street renames, new streets and changed ranges. Keyed by TIGER's edge id (TLID).

accepted.name: Overture Maps Foundation places
accepted.attribution: Places data from the Overture Maps Foundation (overturemaps.org), under CDLA Permissive 2.0 (some of its sources under Apache 2.0); the licence text is in LICENSES/.
accepted.query: SELECT id AS key, names.primary AS name, {cls} AS cls, bbox.ymin AS lat, bbox.xmin AS lon FROM read_parquet('{src}', hive_partitioning = 1) WHERE bbox.xmin BETWEEN {west} AND {east} AND bbox.ymin BETWEEN {south} AND {north} AND confidence >= 0.6 AND COALESCE(CAST({status} AS VARCHAR), '') <> 'permanently_closed'
accepted.history: From the first build on; earlier monthly releases are merged first (overture_seed_releases) while Overture still keeps them in its bucket. Keyed by the GERS id. The newest release is found from the bucket's list. A place Overture marks permanently closed is closed at its last month.
accepted.notes: Overture renamed its category columns in 2026 ("categories" became "taxonomy" and "basic_category"): the build reads the release's columns first and uses taxonomy.primary, else basic_category, else the old categories.primary. Places whose operating_status is "permanently_closed" are left out of the month's data, so their earlier record stays, closed at the last build that listed them open.

accepted.name: Foursquare Open Source Places
accepted.attribution: Foursquare Open Source Places, Copyright 2024 Foursquare Labs, Inc., under the Apache License 2.0 (NOTICE and licence text in LICENSES/).
accepted.query: SELECT fsq_place_id AS key, name, COALESCE(fsq_category_labels[1], '') AS cls, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon, CAST(date_created AS VARCHAR) AS first, CAST(date_closed AS VARCHAR) AS last FROM read_parquet('{src}') WHERE longitude BETWEEN {west} AND {east} AND latitude BETWEEN {south} AND {north}
accepted.history: The dates Foursquare records: when a place was created and when it closed (date_closed), so closed businesses are kept closed. Keyed by fsq_place_id.
accepted.prepare_query: SELECT fsq_place_id, name, fsq_category_labels, latitude, longitude, date_created, date_closed FROM read_parquet('{src}') WHERE country IN ({countries})
accepted.local_query: SELECT fsq_place_id AS key, name, COALESCE(fsq_category_labels[1], '') AS cls, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon, CAST(date_created AS VARCHAR) AS first, CAST(date_closed AS VARCHAR) AS last FROM read_parquet('{src}') WHERE longitude BETWEEN {west} AND {east} AND latitude BETWEEN {south} AND {north}
accepted.notes: Foursquare's files are not sorted by place, so the prepare job reads them once for every covered country and each region takes its box from that local copy (one download instead of one per region).

accepted.name: USGS Geographic Names Information System
accepted.short: the USGS Geographic Names Information System
accepted.attribution: Names from the U.S. Geological Survey's Geographic Names Information System (public domain).
accepted.history: The current names, and older names as they change.
accepted.notes: Cemeteries have their own class (cemetery). Military features (forts, camps, bases, many of them gone) are kept as landmarks; GNIS marks a feature that no longer exists with "(historical)" in its name, and that name is kept as it is, so a lookup says "Fort Example (historical)".

accepted.name: NCES public school locations
accepted.short: the National Center for Education Statistics
accepted.attribution: School locations from the National Center for Education Statistics (EDGE), U.S. Department of Education (public domain).
accepted.history: School years from the first build on.
accepted.notes: The EDGE geocode download holds a shapefile (no CSV): read as points, split per state by its box.

accepted.name: IMLS Public Libraries Survey outlets
accepted.short: the Institute of Museum and Library Services
accepted.attribution: Public library locations from the Institute of Museum and Library Services' Public Libraries Survey (public domain).
accepted.history: The newest survey year from the first build on (each year's file can seed earlier years).
accepted.notes: The newest outlet file is found on IMLS's survey page each build (no hand step). Central and branch libraries only; bookmobiles and books-by-mail have no fixed place.

accepted.name: National Register of Historic Places
accepted.short: the National Register of Historic Places
accepted.attribution: Historic places from the National Park Service's National Register of Historic Places (public domain).
accepted.history: Each property from the month it was listed (the certification date, from 1966 on); keyed by its NRIS reference number.
accepted.notes: Read from the National Park Service's Cultural Resources GIS service (no key). The listing date is not the building's age: a picture older than the listing still gets the name, said "no older record".

accepted.name: USGS Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US)
accepted.attribution: Protected areas from the U.S. Geological Survey's PAD-US (public domain).
accepted.history: Areas as published in the current PAD-US release, from the year established when it is given.

fetch.where: Unit_Nm IS NOT NULL AND Unit_Nm <> '' AND ((Category IN ('Fee','Designation') AND Pub_Access IN ('OA','RA') AND GIS_Acres >= 10) OR Des_Tp IN ('SP','SREC','SHCA','SW') OR Unit_Nm LIKE '%State Forest%')

accepted.notes: Read from USGS's PAD-US 4.1 service (no key). Every state park, state recreation area, state historic or cultural area, state wilderness and state forest, of any size; other named areas of at least 10 acres that are owned or designated (no easements, which are often private land) and open or restricted to the public. Outlines simplified to about 50 m. Vermont gets 61 state parks and Ohio 89.

accepted.name: FAA airports (NASR)
accepted.attribution: Airports from the Federal Aviation Administration's National Airspace System Resources, from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: Each public-use airport from its FAA activation date; updated every 28-day cycle.
accepted.notes: Only public-use facilities that are open: private strips and heliports, often at homes, are left out.

accepted.name: BTS National Transportation Atlas: Amtrak stations
accepted.attribution: Stations from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' National Transportation Atlas Database (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on.
accepted.notes: Train stations only (Amtrak's bus stops are left out).

accepted.name: Public transit stops (GTFS feeds of the Mobility Database catalogue)
accepted.attribution: Transit stops from the agencies' GTFS feeds listed in the pack, each under its own open licence, found through the Mobility Database (mobilitydatabase.org).
accepted.history: From the first build on. Keyed by feed and stop id.

accepted.name: Wikidata
accepted.attribution: Names, coordinates and dates from Wikidata (CC0).
accepted.history: Wikidata's own start and end dates (inception P571, start P580, dissolved or demolished P576, end P582), often decades back.
accepted.notes: Classes kept include lighthouses and light stations, forts and fortifications, military, air, naval and Coast Guard bases and stations, national cemeteries, state parks, current and former railway stations, ski areas, amusement parks, theatres, cinemas, hotels, shopping centres, department stores, factories, mills, mines, breweries, trading posts and ghost towns, each with its inception and closing dates when Wikidata has them. The fine type is the English label of the item's class.

accepted.name: Canadian Geographical Names Database
accepted.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada (Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Geographical Names Database).
accepted.history: Current names; older names as they change.

accepted.name: Statistics Canada open databases of educational, healthcare and cultural and art facilities
accepted.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada (Statistics Canada: The Open Database of Educational Facilities, of Healthcare Facilities, and of Cultural and Art Facilities).
accepted.history: Releases as published.
accepted.notes: Downloaded from Statistics Canada's Linkable Open Data Environment (ODEF 2.1, ODHF 1.1, ODCAF 1.0) at each build (no hand step); split by province.

accepted.name: Base Adresse Nationale (France)
accepted.attribution: Base Adresse Nationale (adresse.data.gouv.fr), Licence Ouverte 2.0, with the date of the file used.
accepted.history: From the first build; the BAN's dated archives on adresse.data.gouv.fr can seed earlier years (one a year).

accepted.name: Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen (Netherlands)
accepted.attribution: Addresses from the Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen (Kadaster, CC0).

fetch.note: Put a CSV export of the BAG address points (latitude, longitude, huisnummer, openbare_ruimte, woonplaats) in inputs/bag/.

accepted.history: From the first build; the BAG keeps the history of every address itself (start and end dates), which can seed it.

accepted.name: OS Open Names (Great Britain)
accepted.attribution: Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database right (OS Open Names, Open Government Licence v3.0).

fetch.note: Put the OS Open Names CSV files, converted to latitude and longitude (they are in British National Grid), in inputs/os-open-names/.

accepted.history: Quarterly releases from the first build on.

accepted.name: NZ Addresses (Toitū Te Whenua LINZ)
accepted.attribution: Sourced from the LINZ Data Service and licensed for reuse under CC BY 4.0 (NZ Addresses).

fetch.note: The LINZ Data Service needs a free account; put the NZ Addresses CSV (WGS84) in inputs/linz/.

accepted.history: From the first build; LINZ publishes changesets that can seed earlier dates.

accepted.name: New Zealand Gazetteer
accepted.attribution: Place names from the New Zealand Gazetteer (Toitū Te Whenua LINZ), CC BY 4.0.

fetch.note: Put the gazetteer CSV in inputs/nz-gazetteer/.

accepted.history: Official names with their dates as published.

accepted.name: CartoCiudad (Spain)
accepted.attribution: CartoCiudad CC-BY 4.0 scne.es (Instituto Geográfico Nacional de España).

fetch.note: CartoCiudad downloads come from the CNIG download centre per province; put the address points as CSV (latitude, longitude, numero, via, municipio) in inputs/cartociudad/.

accepted.history: From the first build.

accepted.name: Gazetteer of Australia
accepted.attribution: Place names from the Gazetteer of Australia (Intergovernmental Committee on Surveying and Mapping), CC BY 4.0.

fetch.note: Put the Gazetteer of Australia CSV in inputs/au-gazetteer/.

accepted.history: Current names.

accepted.name: New York City restaurant inspections (DOHMH)
accepted.attribution: Restaurant inspection results from the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH), NYC Open Data dataset 43nn-pn8j; names, positions and inspection dates only.

queries.select: camis AS key, dba AS name, max(cuisine_description) AS cuisine, max(latitude) AS lat, max(longitude) AS lon, min(inspection_date) AS first, max(inspection_date) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open. DOHMH keeps about three years of inspections.
accepted.notes: New establishments not yet inspected carry the date 1900-01-01 and are left out until their first inspection.

accepted.name: New York State food service establishment inspections (NYSDOH)
accepted.short: the New York State Department of Health
accepted.attribution: Food service establishment inspections from the New York State Department of Health (health.data.ny.gov, datasets 2hcc-shji and aaxz-j6pj); names, positions and inspection dates only.

queries.select: nys_health_operation_id AS key, operation_name AS name, max(latitude) AS lat, max(longitude) AS lon, min(date_of_inspection) AS first, max(date_of_inspection) AS last
nys_health_operation_id AS key, operation_name AS name, max(latitude) AS lat, max(longitude) AS lon, min(date_of_inspection) AS first, max(date_of_inspection) AS last, 'yes' AS closed

accepted.history: Inspections from 2005 on, outside New York City (which has its own): the active and the inactive (closed) establishments, each with its earliest and latest inspection; a closed one keeps its last inspection as its last month.
accepted.notes: The operators' personal names in the source are not read.

accepted.name: Austin, Texas food establishment inspection scores
accepted.attribution: Food establishment inspections from the City of Austin, Texas (data.austintexas.gov, dataset ecmv-9xxi), public domain.

queries.select: facility_id AS key, restaurant_name AS name, max(lat) AS latitude, max(lng) AS longitude, min(inspection_date) AS first, max(inspection_date) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open.

accepted.name: Delaware food establishment inspections
accepted.short: the Delaware Division of Public Health
accepted.attribution: Food establishment inspections from the Delaware Department of Health and Social Services, Division of Public Health, Office of Food Protection (data.delaware.gov, dataset 384s-wygj), public domain.

queries.select: restname AS name, restaddress AS address, geocoded_column AS point, min(insp_date) AS first, max(insp_date) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open.
accepted.notes: The dataset has no permit number: records are keyed by name and street address.

accepted.name: Montgomery County, Maryland food inspections
accepted.attribution: Food inspections from Montgomery County, Maryland, Department of Health and Human Services (data.montgomerycountymd.gov, dataset dkrp-gr48), public domain.

queries.select: registration_number AS key, business_name AS name, location AS point, min(inspection_start_date) AS first, max(inspection_start_date) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open. This dataset starts in July 2024.
accepted.notes: The owner column of the source is not read.

accepted.name: Boulder County, Colorado restaurant inspections 2013-2025
accepted.attribution: Restaurant inspections from Boulder County Public Health, Colorado (data.colorado.gov, dataset tuvj-xz3m), public domain.

queries.select: facilityid AS key, facilityname AS name, location AS point, min(inspectiondate) AS first, max(inspectiondate) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open. The dataset ends in 2025 (a later dataset, 6ytb-f2cq, has other columns).

accepted.name: Cincinnati food safety program inspections
accepted.attribution: Food safety inspections from the City of Cincinnati, Ohio (data.cincinnati-oh.gov, dataset rg6p-b3h3), public domain.

queries.select: license_no AS key, business_name AS name, max(latitude) AS lat, max(longitude) AS lon, min(action_date) AS first, max(action_date) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open.

accepted.name: Baton Rouge retail food inspections
accepted.attribution: Retail food inspections from the Louisiana Department of Health, Office of Public Health, published by the City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge (data.brla.gov, dataset ux2t-b9wr), public domain.

queries.select: permitid AS key, permitname AS name, geocoded_column AS point, min(inspectiondate) AS first, max(inspectiondate) AS last

accepted.history: Each establishment's earliest and latest inspection dates (one record per permit and name, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its own dates); one inspected within the last two years is taken as still open.

accepted.name: San Francisco health inspection scores 2016-2019
accepted.short: San Francisco's Department of Public Health
accepted.attribution: Health inspection scores (2016-2019) from the San Francisco Department of Public Health (data.sfgov.org, dataset pyih-qa8i), Open Data Commons PDDL.

queries.select: business_id AS key, business_name AS name, max(business_latitude) AS lat, max(business_longitude) AS lon, min(inspection_date) AS first, max(inspection_date) AS last

accepted.history: A closed dataset (2016 to 2019): each establishment's first and last inspection in those years.

accepted.name: New York State Liquor Authority licences (active and inactive)
accepted.short: the New York State Liquor Authority
accepted.attribution: Licences of the New York State Liquor Authority, Division of Alcoholic Beverage Control (data.ny.gov, datasets 9s3h-dpkz and 6dg3-2z7i); trade names, positions and dates only.

queries.select: licensepermitid AS key, dba, legalname, description AS kind, georeference AS point, originalissuedate AS first, expirationdate AS last
queries.where: statename = 'New York' AND georeference IS NOT NULL

queries.select: license_permit_id AS key, dba, legalname, description AS kind, georeference AS point, original_issue_date AS first, expiration_date AS last, 'yes' AS closed
queries.where: state_name = 'New York' AND georeference IS NOT NULL

accepted.history: Each licence from its original issue date; an inactive licence ends at its expiry. Keyed by the licence number, so a new licence at the same address is a separate dated record.
accepted.notes: Only premises open to the public (restaurants, bars, shops, hotels, wineries and breweries); additional bars, wholesalers, importers, direct shippers and temporary permits are left out. The trade name is used, or the licensee's name when there is none; a licensee name that looks like a person's ("Surname, Given") is left out.

accepted.name: Colorado liquor licences (current and recently expired)
accepted.attribution: Liquor licences from the Colorado Department of Revenue, Liquor Enforcement Division (data.colorado.gov, datasets ier5-5ms2 and pwjb-9dd5), public domain.

queries.select: license_number AS key, doing_business_as AS dba, licensee_name AS legalname, license_type AS kind, location AS point, expiration AS last
licensenumber AS key, doingbusinessas AS dba, companyname AS legalname, licensetype AS kind, geo AS point, expirationdate AS last, 'yes' AS closed

accepted.history: From the first build on (the datasets have no issue date); an expired or surrendered licence ends at its expiry. Keyed by the licence number.
accepted.notes: Only premises open to the public; permits, wholesalers, importers and direct shippers are left out. A licensee name that looks like a person's is left out.

accepted.name: San Francisco registered business locations
accepted.short: the City and County of San Francisco
accepted.attribution: Registered business locations from the City and County of San Francisco, Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector (data.sfgov.org, dataset g8m3-pdis), Open Data Commons PDDL.

queries.select: uniqueid AS key, dba_name AS name, self_reported_naics_code AS naics, location AS point, location_start_date AS first, location_end_date AS last
queries.where: location IS NOT NULL AND city = 'San Francisco' AND self_reported_naics_code IS NOT NULL AND dba_name IS NOT NULL

accepted.history: Each business location's own start and end dates, back to the 1960s; keyed by the location's id, so a business that moved or was renamed keeps its old record with its dates.
accepted.notes: Only storefront business types (restaurants, bars, shops, hotels and motels (not short-term rentals or bed and breakfasts), petrol stations, garages, salons, laundries, banks, cinemas, gyms; by NAICS code) and only the business's trade name (dba_name): offices, contractors and home services, which are often registered at a home address, and owners' names are left out.

accepted.name: Los Angeles businesses (active and closed)
accepted.attribution: Business locations from the City of Los Angeles Office of Finance (data.lacity.org, dataset r4uk-afju), CC0.

queries.select: location_account AS key, dba_name AS name, naics, location AS point, location_start_date AS first, location_end_date AS last
queries.where: dba_name IS NOT NULL AND naics IS NOT NULL AND location IS NOT NULL

accepted.history: Each business location's own start and end dates; keyed by the location account, so a renamed or moved business keeps its old record with its dates.
accepted.notes: Only storefront business types (by NAICS code) and only the trade name (dba_name), as for San Francisco; the placeholder position 34.0, -118.0 is left out.

accepted.name: New York City consumer licences of storefront businesses (DCWP)
accepted.short: New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
accepted.attribution: Licences issued by the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), NYC Open Data dataset w7w3-xahh; trade names, positions and dates only.

queries.select: license_nbr AS key, dba_trade_name AS name, business_category AS kind, latitude AS lat, longitude AS lon, license_creation_date AS first, lic_expir_dd AS last, case(license_status IN ('Close', 'Out of Business', 'Revoked', 'Surrendered', 'Voided'), 'yes', true, '') AS closed
queries.where: license_type = 'Premises' AND latitude > 1 AND dba_trade_name IS NOT NULL

accepted.history: Each licence from its creation date to its expiry or closing; keyed by the licence number.
accepted.notes: Only premises licences of storefront businesses, and only their trade names: home improvement contractors, individual licences (vendors, drivers, guides) and licences without a trade name, which would show a person's name or home address, are left out.

accepted.name: FDIC bank branch locations
accepted.attribution: Bank branch locations from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation's BankFind Suite (api.fdic.gov), public domain.
accepted.history: Every open branch under its bank's name since the bank took it over (ACQDATE), or since the branch opened (ESTYMD), often decades back. Keyed by the branch's FDIC number, so a branch taken over by another bank keeps its earlier bank's name with its dates from the first build on.
accepted.notes: The API needs no key ("users are currently not required to register"); it does not answer HEAD requests, so its version is the build month.

accepted.name: Food Standards Agency food hygiene ratings (UK)
accepted.attribution: Contains Food Standards Agency data © Crown copyright and database right (food hygiene rating data, ratings.food.gov.uk), Open Government Licence v3.0.
accepted.history: The establishments rated now, each from its latest rating date (they are listed while they trade), then month by month from the first build; keyed by the FHRS id. England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland (FHIS).
accepted.notes: Read from the FSA's open data files (one XML file per local authority, no key or login). Only restaurants, pubs, takeaways, shops and hotels: mobile caterers, home caterers, childminders and care premises, which may be private homes, are left out. No ratings or scores are kept.

accepted.name: Sands & McDougall business directories of Victoria, 1896-1974
accepted.attribution: Historical Business Listings from Sands & McDougall directories, © State of Victoria (Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action), CC BY 4.0.
accepted.history: The directory years (about every ten years, 1896 to 1974) each business was listed in at its address: from the first to the last listing. Melbourne and Victoria only.
accepted.notes: About 550,000 listings from the Victoria Unearthed project, geocoded by the Victorian government; read page by page from its WFS service (no login). Some listings are tradespeople's names as printed in the directories (1896 to 1974).

accepted.name: GeoNames
accepted.attribution: Place names from GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0.
accepted.history: The current names, from the first build on (GeoNames keeps no dates).
accepted.notes: A fallback for the countries outside North America (the US and Canada have GNIS and the Canadian names): lakes, bays, mountains, islands, parks, quarters of towns, churches, castles, monuments, museums, schools, hospitals, stations and airports, from the per-country files (no login).

accepted.name: BTS National Transportation Atlas: ferry terminals
accepted.attribution: Ferry terminals from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on.

accepted.name: FHWA National Bridge Inventory (historic and long bridges)
accepted.attribution: Bridges of the Federal Highway Administration's National Bridge Inventory, from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: Each bridge from the year it was built.
accepted.notes: The inventory has no bridge names, so each is named by what it carries and crosses ("Middle Rd bridge over Hudson Brook"). Only bridges on or eligible for the National Register and bridges at least 150 m long are kept (about 270 in Vermont and 1,100 in Ohio, of 4,500 and 32,000).

accepted.name: USACE National Inventory of Dams (named dams)
accepted.short: the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
accepted.attribution: Dams of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' National Inventory of Dams, from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD), a work of the United States government (public domain).

fetch.where: name IS NOT NULL AND name <> ''

accepted.history: Each dam from the year it was completed.
accepted.notes: Named dams only (about 770 in Vermont and 1,700 in Ohio). Owners' names are not read.

accepted.name: DoD military installations, ranges and training areas (MIRTA)
accepted.attribution: Military installations of the Department of Defense (MIRTA), from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics' National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: Active installations from the first build on.

accepted.name: National Park Service points of interest
accepted.attribution: Points of interest from the National Park Service's public datasets (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on.
accepted.notes: Read from the NPS public datasets service (no API key). Each name carries its park ("Visitor Center (Saint-Gaudens National Historical Park)"), since many are generic. Only named places a photo can show: trailheads, campgrounds, visitor centres, overlooks, peaks, waterfalls, historic buildings and sites, monuments; parking lots, restrooms, mile markers and benches are left out.

accepted.name: US Forest Service recreation sites
accepted.attribution: Recreation sites from the US Forest Service's Enterprise Data Warehouse (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on.
accepted.notes: Read from the Forest Service's EDW map service (no RIDB key). Existing developed sites only; recreation residences (private cabins), dispersed camping spots and single camp units are left out.

accepted.name: NCES private school locations (PSS)
accepted.short: the National Center for Education Statistics
accepted.attribution: Private school locations from the National Center for Education Statistics (EDGE, Private School Universe Survey), U.S. Department of Education (public domain).
accepted.history: The newest survey (every two years) from the first build on; older survey files can seed closures.

accepted.name: NCES postsecondary school locations (IPEDS)
accepted.short: the National Center for Education Statistics
accepted.attribution: Colleges and universities from the National Center for Education Statistics (EDGE, IPEDS), U.S. Department of Education (public domain).
accepted.history: The newest school year from the first build on; older files can seed closures.

accepted.name: Atlas of Historical County Boundaries (Newberry Library)
accepted.short: the Newberry Library's Atlas of Historical County Boundaries
accepted.attribution: Atlas of Historical County Boundaries, Dr. William M. Scholl Center for American History and Culture, The Newberry Library.
accepted.history: Every version of every county and its boundaries since the first colonial counties, each with the exact dates it held (to 2000; the versions current in 2000 are taken as current).
accepted.notes: Non-county areas (unorganised land) are left out. Lookups give the county as it was on the picture's date. The national file (generalised to about 100 m) has shifted offsets inside its .zip, which the build repairs. The Newberry's terms: "available ... for any lawful purpose, commercial or non-commercial, without licensing or permission fees"; the older Creative Commons note inside the file is superseded.

accepted.name: Pennsylvania historical markers (PHMC)
accepted.short: the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission
accepted.attribution: Historical markers of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (data.pa.gov, dataset xt8f-pzzz), public domain.

queries.select: id AS key, name, latitude, longitude, dedicateddate AS first

accepted.history: Each marker from its dedication date (from 1914 on).

accepted.name: Washington, DC basic business licences (storefronts)
accepted.attribution: Basic Business Licenses from the District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection (opendata.dc.gov), CC BY 4.0.

fetch.where: LICENSETYPE = 'Business License' AND PREMISEINDC = 'Yes' AND ENTITYTRADENAME IS NOT NULL AND BUSINESSACTIVITY IN ('Restaurant','Delicatessen','Grocery Store','Hotel','Beauty Shop','Barber Shop','Beauty Shop (Nails)','Gasoline Dealer','Dry Cleaner','Bakery','Parking Facility','Motor Vehicle Dealer','Consumer Goods (Auto Repair)','Secondhand Dealer (Class A)','Public Hall','Power Laundry')

accepted.history: Each licence from its first issue date to its end (an expired one ends there); keyed by the customer number, so a renamed business keeps its old name with its dates.
accepted.notes: Only premises in DC of storefront activities, under their trade names: rentals (one- and two-family, short-term and vacation rentals, rooming houses), contractors, salespeople and owners' and agents' names are left out.

accepted.name: Minneapolis food inspections
accepted.attribution: Food inspections from the City of Minneapolis (opendata.minneapolismn.gov); the City has waived all copyright and related rights to its open data.
accepted.history: Each establishment's first and last inspection, one record per licence and name.

accepted.name: USCG Light List: lighthouses and major lights
accepted.short: the U.S. Coast Guard Light List
accepted.attribution: Lighthouses from the U.S. Coast Guard Light List, Volumes I-VII (Navigation Center), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: The lights listed now, from the first build on (the Light List has no dates; lighthouse dates come from Wikidata).
accepted.notes: Read from the Navigation Center's Light List volumes I-VII: the XML files when the Light List page offers them, else the text PDFs, read with pypdf (no OCR: the volumes are text; a scanned volume is reported and left out). Only lights named "... Light" whose structure is a tower, house or lighthouse are kept; buoys, daybeacons, range lights and lights on skeleton towers, poles, posts, dolphins or spindles are left out. Positions are converted from the list's degrees, minutes and seconds. navcen.uscg.gov refused requests from the development sandbox (403); the build tries from GitHub Actions and reports "skipped (could not be downloaded: ...)" when it is refused there too.

accepted.name: USACE Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS)
accepted.short: the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
accepted.attribution: Formerly Used Defense Sites from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (FUDS program, FY24), a work of the United States government (public domain).

fetch.where: ELIGIBILITY = 'Eligible' AND FEATURENAME IS NOT NULL

accepted.history: Former military properties (forts, camps, airfields, depots, ranges), named as former sites; the layer has no dates of DoD use, so the record runs from the first build.
accepted.notes: About 10,000 properties nationally, keyed by the FUDS property number; only those eligible for the program (the DoD did own or use them). The current owners' names are not read. The dates of DoD use appear only in free-text descriptions, which are not parsed; Wikidata gives dates for the better-known forts and bases.

accepted.name: VA national cemeteries
accepted.attribution: National cemetery locations from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (datahub.va.gov, dataset fcxt-zc8r), a work of the United States government (public domain).
accepted.history: From the first build on (Wikidata gives the national cemeteries' founding dates).
accepted.notes: Cemetery sites only (about 150): never burial or gravesite records.

accepted.name: OpenHistoricalMap
accepted.attribution: Historical places from OpenHistoricalMap contributors (openhistoricalmap.org), CC0; features with their own licence tag are left out.
accepted.history: Each feature's own start and end dates as mapped in OpenHistoricalMap (old businesses, buildings, stations, forts, mills), often a century back or more.
accepted.notes: Read from OHM's Overpass API, one query per region (OHM's planet files are archived and cannot be downloaded). Named nodes and ways with a start or end date, as points (a way at its centre); lines (streets, railway lines, rivers), boundaries and relations are left out. OHM's data is CC0 except features carrying their own licence tag, which are left out. About 1,900 features in Vermont's box and 34,000 in Ohio's.

accepted.name: Statistics Canada Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities
accepted.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada (Statistics Canada, The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities) and the municipal open data listed in its sources.
accepted.history: The 2021 release (one edition so far).
accepted.notes: Named facilities only (parks, arenas, pools, fields, playgrounds); paths and trails, which are lines, are left out. About 114,000 records in Ontario and 22,000 in British Columbia before that.

accepted.name: Aboriginal Lands of Canada Legislative Boundaries (Canada Lands Survey System)
accepted.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada (Natural Resources Canada, Canada Lands Survey System: Aboriginal Lands of Canada Legislative Boundaries).
accepted.history: From the first build on.
accepted.notes: About 3,400 Indian reserves, settlements and other Aboriginal lands, as areas (class region: named areas, not towns).

accepted.name: Toronto DineSafe food premises inspections
accepted.attribution: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Toronto (DineSafe, Toronto Public Health).
accepted.history: Each food premises' first and last inspection in the current file (about two years), one record per establishment and name.
accepted.notes: Only the establishment's name, position and inspection dates are read (no infractions or fines).

accepted.name: Boston food establishment licences and inspections
accepted.attribution: Food establishment inspections from the City of Boston (data.boston.gov), Open Data Commons PDDL.

queries: SELECT licenseno AS key, businessname AS name, max(descript) AS kind, min(issdttm) AS first, max(expdttm) AS last, max(location) AS point FROM "4582bec6-2b4f-4f9e-bc55-cbaa73117f4c" WHERE location IS NOT NULL AND businessname IS NOT NULL GROUP BY licenseno, businessname ORDER BY licenseno, businessname

accepted.history: Each food licence from its issue date to its expiry (about 9,900 licences since 2006), one record per licence and name.
accepted.notes: The inspection file is grouped by the portal itself to one row per licence and name; the owners' names and the violations are never read.

accepted.name: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian areas
accepted.attribution: American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian areas from the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles (public domain).
accepted.history: The current year's areas (seed years possible like the other TIGER layers).

rejected.name: Google, Bing, Yelp, Apple and most commercial business directories
rejected.reason: No redistribution allowed.

rejected.name: Wikipedia text
rejected.reason: Share-alike text; only Wikidata's CC0 names, coordinates and dates are used.

rejected.name: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints
rejected.reason: Open, but about 130 million US buildings would make the packs several times larger; not used for now (could be a third, optional part later).

rejected.name: HIFLD Open
rejected.reason: DHS shut HIFLD Open down in August 2025; its layers come from the original agencies, which are used directly (NCES, IMLS, FAA, BTS, NPS).

rejected.name: CMS Hospital General Information
rejected.reason: Has addresses but no coordinates; hospitals come from OpenStreetMap, GNIS, Overture and Foursquare.

rejected.name: County assessor and parcel websites directly
rejected.reason: Terms differ county by county and many forbid redistribution; their open address data reaches the packs through the NAD and OpenAddresses, whose per-source terms are known. Not scraped.

rejected.name: NAD data of HI, MI, MN, NH, OR, SC, SD (and parts of CO, IL, KS, MD, ND)
rejected.reason: Left out until each state's terms are checked; OpenAddresses sources with open licences can fill in.

rejected.name: OpenAddresses sources with share-alike or non-commercial licences
rejected.licence: CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, ODbL (per source)
rejected.reason: Share-alike or non-commercial terms would bind the whole address layer.

rejected.name: Overture Maps addresses and buildings themes
rejected.reason: Addresses duplicate the NAD and OpenAddresses with mixed terms; buildings are large and partly OpenStreetMap.

rejected.name: OpenStreetMap full history and Geofabrik internal history extracts
rejected.reason: Open, but the planet history is about 150 GB and Geofabrik's per-state history extracts need an OpenStreetMap login; OpenStreetMap history starts at the first build.

rejected.name: Statistics Canada Open Database of Buildings and CanVec
rejected.reason: Open, but mostly unnamed shapes; named features come from the Canadian Geographical Names Database.

rejected.name: National Road Network (Canada)
rejected.reason: Open; not used yet (street names come from OpenStreetMap and the ODA). A later addition for Canadian address ranges.

rejected.name: GTFS feeds without a licence or with non-commercial or no-derivatives terms
rejected.reason: Unclear or restrictive terms.

rejected.name: Statewide address portals not in the NAD
rejected.reason: None added yet: each needs its licence checked (candidates: Minnesota, Michigan, Oregon, South Carolina address points). Add a state with an entry like openaddresses once its licence is confirmed open.

rejected.name: Ireland: Eircode
rejected.reason: Not open.

rejected.name: UK: OS AddressBase and Royal Mail PAF
rejected.reason: Not open; OS Open UPRN is open but has no address text, so it adds nothing to names.

rejected.name: Marine Regions IHO Sea Areas v3
rejected.reason: Non-commercial and share-alike; the program uses Natural Earth's public-domain marine names.

rejected.name: Chicago food inspections, business licences and other City of Chicago data
rejected.licence: City of Chicago Data Terms of Use
rejected.reason: The terms let the City require anyone to stop all display and distribution of the data at any time, ask for an indemnity, and require a disclaimer on every site that redistributes it: not an open licence.

rejected.name: Seattle and King County: food establishment inspections (r878-4sxa) and active business licences (wnbq-64tb)
rejected.reason: Open, but neither dataset has coordinates (addresses only); geocoding them is not simple enough.

rejected.name: Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission licences (data.texas.gov 7hf9-qc9f) and Mixed Beverage receipts
rejected.reason: No coordinates (addresses only) and no licence stated on the dataset.

rejected.name: Iowa, Connecticut and Washington State liquor licences
rejected.reason: No dataset of licensed premises with coordinates was found on data.iowa.gov or data.ct.gov (Connecticut publishes brand registrations and suspensions only); Washington's LCB datasets are renewal and local authority notices, not a premises list.

rejected.name: Montgomery County, Maryland food inspections before July 2024 (5pue-gfbe), Prince George's County food inspections, Dallas restaurant inspections
rejected.reason: No licence is stated on these datasets (Montgomery County's newer dataset, which is marked public domain, is used).

rejected.name: Marin County food facility inspections and active business licences
rejected.reason: Share-alike; only OpenStreetMap's own layer may be ODbL in a pack.

rejected.name: Kansas City, Providence, Cincinnati and Delaware business licences
rejected.reason: Open, but without storefront categories that keep home-based businesses out (Delaware's are mostly contractors), or without dates (Kansas City, Providence).

rejected.name: Netherlands KVK Handelsregister
rejected.reason: Not open.

rejected.name: Belgium KBO/BCE open data
rejected.reason: The bulk files need a registered account.

rejected.name: Denmark CVR (Erhvervsstyrelsen)
rejected.reason: Bulk and API access need a registered username and password.

rejected.name: Norway Enhetsregisteret (Brønnøysund)
rejected.reason: Open, but addresses without coordinates; Norway's address register is not in the catalogue yet, so it cannot be geocoded cheaply.

rejected.name: Australia ABN bulk extract (data.gov.au)
rejected.reason: No addresses with coordinates (state and postcode only), and many entries are individuals.

rejected.name: New Zealand Companies Office register
rejected.reason: The API needs a subscription key.

rejected.name: Kitchener, Ontario: Historical Vernon City Directories Mapped (University of Waterloo Library)
rejected.reason: The project page offers the geocoded CSV files but states no licence (the directory scans came from partners); not used unless the Library publishes an open licence.

rejected.name: Pleiades
rejected.reason: Open, but ancient-world places (mostly before AD 640) rarely name where a photo was taken.

rejected.name: World Historical Gazetteer
rejected.reason: No single bulk download under one open licence; each contributed dataset has its own terms and some downloads need a login.

rejected.name: Library of Congress Sanborn fire insurance maps
rejected.reason: Scanned map images, with no point data of buildings or businesses to read.

rejected.name: USDA National Farmers Market Directory
rejected.reason: Its download now goes through the USDA Local Food Portal API, which needs a key.

rejected.name: IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File
rejected.reason: Addresses but no coordinates; geocoding them against NAD or TIGER ranges is not simple enough yet.

rejected.name: HMdb (the Historical Marker Database)
rejected.reason: Not open; state historic marker lists can be added state by state when an open download exists.

rejected.name: USPS post office locations
rejected.reason: No current official download with coordinates (the HIFLD layer is gone); post offices come from GNIS, OpenStreetMap, Overture and Foursquare.

rejected.name: Denver business, liquor and other City and County of Denver data
rejected.reason: The terms make every user indemnify the City and hold it harmless: not an open licence.

rejected.name: EIA power plants (EIA-860)
rejected.reason: EIA publishes plant locations only as an Excel workbook (not read by the build yet) or through an API that needs a key; the Esri copy of the layer is under the Esri Master License Agreement.

rejected.name: FCC antenna structure registrations and broadcast station lists
rejected.reason: Weekly bulk files of unnamed structures (owners and registration numbers, which are often people); they would not name a place in a picture.

rejected.name: EPA Facility Registry Service
rejected.reason: Millions of regulated sites (many of them farms and homes with a tank or a permit); no lightweight named subset of public places.

rejected.name: Texas Historical Commission markers (THC Atlas)
rejected.reason: THC's published layer states no licence; only a county's copy asks to credit the THC.

rejected.name: Virginia DHR highway markers
rejected.reason: No open download or service of the markers was found on Virginia's portals.

rejected.name: Los Angeles County restaurant inspections
rejected.reason: Only university research copies were found, not an official open layer.

rejected.name: Alaska / Anchorage business licences (DCRA)
rejected.reason: No licence stated, and the statewide list is mostly sole proprietors at home addresses.

rejected.name: New Orleans occupational business licences
rejected.reason: The dataset (data.nola.gov hjcd-grvu) states no licence.

rejected.name: Honolulu, Las Vegas (Southern Nevada Health District), Wake County/Raleigh, Tampa/Hillsborough, Portland and Kansas City business licences or restaurant inspections
rejected.reason: No downloadable dataset with coordinates and an open licence was found on their portals (Kansas City's has no dates).

rejected.name: NPS Maritime Heritage Inventory of Historic Light Stations
rejected.reason: Published as web pages per state, with no downloadable dataset; lighthouse dates come from Wikidata and the Light List gives the current lights.

rejected.name: BRAC (base realignment and closure) installation lists
rejected.reason: No open list with locations and closure years was found; EPA's FRS BRAC layer (125 facilities) has neither closure years nor an open licence statement (EPA Data Licensing Agreement). Closed bases come from FUDS, GNIS and Wikidata (with dates).

rejected.name: A US Coast Guard units or stations layer
rejected.reason: USCG's public GIS (USCG_GIS_Data) publishes waterways and notices, not units; the DoD's MIRTA layer has no Coast Guard sites. Coast Guard stations come from Wikidata (with dates) and GNIS.

rejected.name: VA Facilities API and the NCA Gravesite Locator
rejected.reason: The Facilities API needs a key, and the Gravesite Locator holds burial records, which are never used; the VA's own cemetery-sites dataset is used.

rejected.name: Find a Grave and BillionGraves
rejected.reason: Not open; not used.

rejected.name: State and local cemetery inventories
rejected.reason: None with an open licence and a simple download was found yet; GNIS and OpenStreetMap carry most named cemeteries.

rejected.name: OpenHistoricalMap planet files
rejected.reason: The newest planet file (February 2025) is archived in S3 Glacier and cannot be downloaded (InvalidObjectState); OHM is read through its Overpass API instead.

rejected.name: Parks Canada Federal Heritage Designations (national historic sites, heritage lighthouses and railway stations)
rejected.reason: Has designation dates but no coordinates (street addresses only), and the packs have no address geocoder.

rejected.name: TTB permittees (wineries, breweries, distilleries) and the CMS Provider of Services file
rejected.reason: Addresses without coordinates; placepacks has no address geocoder (lookups go from a position to a name, not back).

rejected.name: National Heritage Areas, BLM recreation sites and Bureau of Reclamation lakes
rejected.reason: No official open service or download was found (only third-party copies); their lands are in PAD-US.

rejected.name: Indigenous Services Canada reserve and land layers (data.sac-isc.gc.ca)
rejected.reason: The same lands come from the Canada Lands Survey System layer, which states the Open Government Licence - Canada.

rejected.name: NPS National Historic Landmarks as a separate layer
rejected.reason: Already in the National Register layer (its Is_NHL flag); not a separate source.

candidates.name: Denmark: Danmarks Adresseregister (DAR)
candidates.note: Open and free; the terms must be checked for redistribution in a combined database.

candidates.name: Belgium: BOSA BeST addresses
candidates.note: Published openly by FPS BOSA; the licence text must be checked.

candidates.name: Germany: the open address data of the Länder (for example NRW, Berlin, Hamburg, Thüringen, Sachsen)
candidates.note: Each Land publishes its own; add the Länder whose licence is dl-de/zero or dl-de/by one by one.

candidates.name: Austria: BEV Adressregister
candidates.note: Add once the current terms are confirmed.

candidates.name: Switzerland: federal building and dwelling register addresses (GWR)
candidates.licence: opendata.swiss open use with attribution (to confirm)
candidates.note: Add once the terms are confirmed.

candidates.name: Norway: Kartverket address data (Matrikkelen)
candidates.note: Add once confirmed.

candidates.name: Finland: DVV buildings and addresses
candidates.note: Add once confirmed.

candidates.name: Sweden, Iceland, Portugal, Italy (ANNCSU): national address registers
candidates.note: Later.

candidates.name: Australia: G-NAF
candidates.licence: Open G-NAF EULA (CC BY 4.0 based, with a mail-use restriction)
candidates.note: The extra restriction must be passed on; decide after reading the full EULA.

candidates.name: Japan: Address Base Registry (Digital Agency)
candidates.note: Later.

candidates.name: GEBCO undersea feature names
candidates.note: Later, for named undersea features.

candidates.name: US Census school districts (UNSD, ELSD, SCSD)
candidates.note: Open; to add like the Census places (areas per state).

candidates.name: Parks Canada places and the open data portals of large Canadian cities and provinces
candidates.licence: OGL-Canada and OGL-type city licences (to confirm per portal)
candidates.note: Add one by one once each licence is confirmed; their addresses already reach the ODA.

candidates.name: Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints as a third, optional part
candidates.note: Possible later as a separate download for inside/outside a building.

candidates.name: France: SIRENE establishments (INSEE) with INSEE's geolocation file
candidates.note: Etalab's geocoded "GeoSIRENE" files were decommissioned in April 2026; INSEE now publishes a separate geolocation file (data.gouv.fr dataset 61d5e2d372a52d9f9411ff88, about 1.2 GB) that has to be joined with the 2 GB stock of establishments for names, NAF codes and dates. To add as a prepared DuckDB join (like Foursquare), keeping only storefront NAF codes, statutDiffusionEtablissement = O, and legal persons (no entrepreneurs individuels).

candidates.name: Other US city health inspections on Socrata (Cambridge MA PDDL, Kansas City food permits, San Mateo, Fulton County GA CC BY)
candidates.licence: PDDL, public domain or CC BY 4.0
candidates.note: Open; can be added as "socrata" entries like the ones used, after checking each one's columns.

candidates.name: Louisville Metro restaurant inspection scores
candidates.note: On an ArcGIS service (LouisvilleMetro, FoodServiceData) that the arcgis method can read; add once the platform's terms are read and confirmed open.

candidates.name: USFS trails and NPS trails
candidates.note: Line layers on the same services as the recreation sites and points of interest; the arcgis method would need line output.

candidates.name: Vancouver business licences 1997-2012 and current
candidates.note: About 959,000 dated licence records with positions; the portal's grouped export (one row per licence) could not be tested from the build sandbox (connection resets). Add as an opendatasoft export entry once tested; use trade names and storefront business types only.

candidates.name: Allegheny County (WPRDC) food facilities; Philadelphia business licences and inspections
candidates.note: WPRDC's food facility list has no queryable table (a grouped SQL query is needed to keep it small); OpenDataPhilly's catalogue API was not reachable from the sandbox.

candidates.name: Calgary, Edmonton, Ottawa, Montreal, Winnipeg, Halifax, Victoria and Mississauga business and food data
candidates.licence: City open government licences (to confirm one by one)
candidates.note: Not checked yet; each is a Socrata, CKAN or ArcGIS portal the existing methods can read.

candidates.name: National Trails System, Wild and Scenic Rivers, NRCan National Road Network and CanVec
candidates.note: Line layers: the arcgis method would need line output (and the NRN is large).

candidates.name: Census school districts (UNSD, ELSD, SCSD), Census urban areas, older TIGER place vintages, older StatCan census subdivisions
candidates.note: School districts need a class the lookup and the Photo Location Identifier would not read as a town, county or trip name; older vintages would seed dated town names like the TIGER seed years.

candidates.name: Open Brewery DB, USGS stream gauges, NOAA tide stations, state rest areas and state park portals
candidates.note: Lower value (state parks already come from PAD-US); check each licence before adding.

candidates.name: Canadian Register of Historic Places, Quebec Répertoire du patrimoine culturel, Ontario AGCO liquor licences
candidates.note: Check each licence and whether it has coordinates.
